1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <string_view>
21	#include <vector>
22	
23	namespace andes_sim {
24	
25	// True for the known command names (run/list/doctor/profile). The single
26	// source of truth shared by the parser (default-command rule) and main's
27	// dispatch.
28	bool is_subcommand(std::string_view name);
29	
30	struct Cli {
31	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
32	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
33	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
34	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
35	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
36	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
37	  // parsed where they are used.
38	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
39	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
40	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
41	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
42	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
43	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)
44	  std::string log_file;                   // --log-file <path> (full trace capture)
45	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
46	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
47	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
48	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
49	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
50	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
51	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)

# Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
#
# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
#
# Usage:
#   make            # build both
#   make clean
#
# Output (in this directory):
#   libhybrid_handoff.so    -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
#   libhotIterationLoop.so  -- hot inner-loop detector (`andesim profile`)

CC ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared
LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)

.PHONY: all clean

all: libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so

libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/write_mask.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)

# hotIterationLoop is standalone: it needs only qemu-plugin.h + glib, not
# HYBRID_INCLUDE.
libhotIterationLoop.so: hotIterationLoop.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotIterationLoop.c $(LIBS)

clean:
	rm -f libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so

# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
fi

hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
  # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
  # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}

# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
hybrid_describe_int() {
  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
}

# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
put_word_le() {
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

- Files: `driver/profile.cpp:432-454` (builder), called `driver/cmd_profile.cpp:362`; contrast `driver/engine_registry.cpp:53-74` (fast-leg + standalone `invoke` templates) filled by `driver/argv.cpp` `build_argv` via `driver/run_plan.cpp:282-298`.

- Why fragile: this is a *second, independently-maintained* copy of the QEMU machine-setup knowledge, and it has **already drifted** from the canonical templates — profile emits `-M`/`-semihosting` (profile.cpp:441-442) while the engine templates emit `-machine`/`-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native` (engine_registry.cpp:58-59,73-74). A future change to the QEMU bring-up shape must be made in two places or profile silently keeps the old shape. The repo itself names this pattern "altitude debt" at `run_plan.hpp:63-69`.
- Weighing → mostly **acceptable as-is**: the genuinely reusable half (engine→`qemu.cfg` probe, `qemu_cpu_from_cfg`, `synced_vlen`) *is* already reused (cmd_profile.cpp:339-357). Routing the argv through `plan_argvs` would drag in the shared-mmap/state-threading context that profile deliberately doesn't have, and adding a `profile-leg` role to `builtin_qemu_arch` would leak profile-plugin param names (`limit=`/`min_iters=`, `-d plugin -D`) into the engine registry — worse altitude, and it touches the F2 contract for a cosmetic gain. **2. Fallback-CPU literal `"andes-ax45mpv"` duplicated in `cmd_profile.cpp` and `run_plan.cpp`.**
- Files: `driver/cmd_profile.cpp:343` and `driver/run_plan.cpp:296`; the concept is already named ("the family default (andes-ax45mpv)") at `driver/run_plan.hpp:37`.
